title: Annotatio IV §.XIX: Taborites closer — tropical Institution; spiritual not natural presence; faith’s mouth
pass_a_gloss: yet Hus’s Followers, from the region in which they lived called Bohemian Brethren, and from a certain town or Castle named Tabor called Taborites, came nearer the truth concerning the Sacred Supper, having recognized both the tropical speech in the Institution words and the presence of Christ’s body in the Supper — but only Spiritual, not Natural and corporal; likewise eating to be performed with the mouth of faith, and hence peculiar to the faithful, not common to unbelievers. All this becomes clear from their various Confessions published in the XIVth and XVth Ages and comprehended by Balthasar Lydius, Pastor of Dordrecht, in the Year 1616 in one Volume of two parts.
pass_b_english: Hus’s followers — Bohemian Brethren / Taborites — came nearer Supper truth.

They recognize tropical Institution speech and Christ’s presence in the Supper — Spiritual only, not natural/corporal — eating by faith’s mouth, for the faithful not the unbelieving (Lydius’s collected confessions, 1616).
source_text: tamen Sectatores Hussi à regione, in qua degebant, Bohemi Fratres, ab oppido quodam, seu Castello, nomine Tabor, Taboritæ nuncupati, veritati de S. Cœna propiores accessere, agnitâ tùm tropicâ in verbis Institutionis locutione, tùm præsentia corporis Christi in Cena, sed Spirituali duntaxat, non Naturali corporalique; manducatione item ore fidei peragendâ, hincque fidelibus peculiari, nec infidelibus communi. Hæc manifesta evadunt omnia ex Confessionibus eorum variis, Seculis XIV. & XV. in publicum editis & à Balthasare Lydro Pastore Dordraceno Anno 1616. unô Volumine, duabus constante partibus, compræhensis.
